metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most of the human messages question the produced output by identifier or decision, e.g. #37 'What is the role of TYPES and frozenset here?', #6 'BlankAsNone sounds almost like some anon process', #24 'genome marker = GenomeDnaMarker?', #45 on logger param typing, #50 on TypeAdapter, #88 'CancerType: type in group mentions a conflict but I don't think covers the resolution?', so at least one could only come from someone who had read the code and docs.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: The git, coding, Python and root CLAUDE.md rules were all in context, and the nine commit subjects follow the required form (lowercase, under 50 characters, no full stops, scope `tools` used and dropped correctly), while the unread backend, frontend and snowflake CLAUDE.md files do not cover the docs, CI and tools/ changes.

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 615 of 1532 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: Median generated lines per producing prompt was 21, below the 50-line band 3 limit, and most requests name a single unit (rename a variable, switch to f-strings, reword one docs passage), though a few bare 'Yes'/'y' approvals accepted 166 to 312 lines.
